SOURCE-ASSISTED READING, 22 September 2026

Base: review-2026-09-22-image-only, preserved unchanged. The current reader saw that record and the earlier F-8bfm report before the following work. Actual manuscript and print images were inspected. This is not an independent image-only reading and not a full-leaf collation.

The original packet image-001.png was inspected again. It comprises the first four rows of c1_lo_s02.jpg, with its top and bottom rows clipped. The parent file's SHA256 was checked and matches the parent SHA256 in the frozen record. Its native crop origin/scale relative to the complete Fragmentarium image remains unrecovered. The cached manuscript strips were already rotated for reading; no new rotation, enhancement, or rescaling was applied. The larger c1_lo.jpg was also opened, but is sideways and was not used for a fresh full transcription.

Notation: parentheses are proposed abbreviation expansions; ? marks doubt; [illegible] preserves unresolved image text. Below, numbers count physical text rows from the top of each named crop, including cropped rows. Overlap between neighboring strips is not additional manuscript text.

The base's suſtā? (substantia?) and talibꝫ? (talibus?) are not retained. The underlined word on row 2 is an abbreviated Aristotle reference. The word order sufficienter / Aristotle is read from the image with the edition present, not inferred to be identical with print; print puts Aristoteles before sufficienter. No deletion or insertion is securely identified. Red underlining is present.

Scope of comparison:
The front-cover lower-band strips c1_lo_s01–03 were compared with actual edition crops p40_a1.jpg and p40_a2.jpg: the question whether theological virtues must be posited beyond acquired moral virtues, Aristotle's discussion of happiness, then assent through natural capacities, love, hope of immortal life, and the need for infused habits. This is connecting commentary, not merely a biblical lemma.
The back-cover lower-band strips c3_lo_s00–04 were compared with p40_b0.jpg and p40_b1.jpg: supernatural virtue, the numbered replies, and the Rectitudo / Gratitudo / Sollicitudo / Altitudo division. The edition visibly heads this part Lectio III. Only the quoted rows and their context were checked, not every abbreviation of the section.
The back-cover upper-band strips c3_up_s01–03 were compared with p41_a0.jpg: heart given liberaliter / integraliter / perpetualiter, followed by lending, selling, and giving it, and service for temporal prosperity. This supplies an additional distinctive passage beyond the initial Aristotle strip. It had appeared in the old report, so it is not held-out evidence.
The low-resolution full print images ed_39.jpg, ed_40.jpg, ed_41.jpg were also inspected for location and headings; detailed word comparisons used the larger print crops. ed_39 contains Lectio II, ed_40 Lectio III, with the selected column-a text preceding that heading. No print folio number was reconstructed from scan indexes.

Differences and uncertainties:
- Manuscript Dubium est hic utrum versus print Primo potest esse dubium hic utrum.
- Manuscript sufficienter? Aristotle order versus print Aristoteles sufficienter.
- Manuscript ille deus dabit versus print deus dabit.
- Manuscript ad istam consequendam versus print ad illam consequendam.
- Manuscript nobis infunduntur and in sola sacra scriptura versus print infunduntur and in sacra scriptura.
- Manuscript hic intelligitur versus print debet intelligi.
- Manuscript ibi repeated in the fourfold division; print gives its terms without each ibi.
- Manuscript Circa primum notandum quod simplicitas ista debet esse cum prudencia versus print Simplicitas autem illa debet esse cum prudentia.
The doubtful manuscript relacione? is not silently rewritten revelatione from print. The former report's proposed homines/hominem difference is not retained: the inspected print crop also appears to abbreviate homines. Neither these variants nor the identification establishes that this manuscript is a better witness.

The old report exposed other proposed sources, but no Google Books snippets, 1509 edition, 1689 reworking, secondary scholarship, or alternative commentary was opened in this review. No OCR file was used in this review. No network retrieval was needed.

Conclusion: identified, high confidence, as the text of Robert Holcot's Super Sapientiam Salomonis, end of Lectio II and part of Lectio III in the Hagenau 1494 edition. Sustained agreements in three connected developments support this identification. Full leaf reconstruction, exact endpoints, all readings, date, provenance, recension, dependence, and witness novelty remain outside this check. No complete alternative compilation was collated. No human palaeographic verification or transcription accuracy score is claimed.
